text.tspan: The ‘Heat Index’ is a measure of how the hot weather "feels" to the body. This table uses relative humidity and air
temperature to produce the "apparent temperature" or the temperature the body "feels". These values are for
shady locations only. Exposure to full sunshine can increase heat index values by up to 15°F. Also, strong winds,
particularly with very hot, dry air, can be extremely hazardous as the wind adds heat to the body.
General Affect on People in High Risk Groups
Sunstroke, heat cramps, or heat exhaustion
